BOB NGUYEN · DISTRICT 4
# Keep Bob Nguyen for Millbrae City Council, District 4. RESPONSIBLE SUSTAINABLE BALANCED ACCOUNTABLE Responsible, sustainable growth. growth.
Responsible, sustainable growth for our city.
Why I'm Staying
My name is Bob Nguyen, and I am the current Councilmember representing Millbrae District 4, where I have served since 2024. My wife, who is Chinese American, and I have called Millbrae home for more than 10 years, raising our family and building deep roots in this community. My commitment to public service began in 2022, when I stepped forward as a write-in candidate to ensure District 4 voters had a real choice, earning 26.69% of the vote — an extraordinary showing that reflected meaningful support from neighbors across the district.
Before joining the Council, I was actively involved in community efforts opposing the La Quinta supportive-housing proposal and supporting the 2024 recall election.
I'm running to keep Millbrae safe, livable, and financially strong while planning responsibly for the future. My approach is balanced, practical, and data-driven — focused on protecting our neighborhoods, strengthening infrastructure, and ensuring City Hall listens to the people it serves.

## Five key pillars for responsible, balanced leadership in Millbrae.
- 01
### Strong, Reliable Infrastructure
Focus city resources on maintaining and upgrading streets, sidewalks, drainage, and utilities before chasing flashy projects.
- 02
### Responsible Spending & Budget Transparency
Spend taxpayer dollars responsibly — fund the basics first, cut waste, and keep the budget open and easy for residents to follow.
- 03
### Thriving Local Businesses & Downtown
Support businesses with predictable rules and clear communication.
- 04
### Safe, Livable Neighborhoods
Maintain a strong focus on public safety while also addressing quality-of-life issues like speeding, noise, and cleanliness.
- 05
### Fair Representation in Regional Decisions
Make sure Millbrae has a strong, informed voice with the region and the boards that affect our housing, transit, and budget.

## Voting in District 4 is simple.
We'll walk you through registration, mail-in ballots, and where to vote in person.
Election Day
November 3, 2026
General Municipal Election — voters in City Council Districts 2 and 4 elect their City Council representatives.
Nomination Period
Jul 13 – Aug 7, 2026
Candidate filing period; closes 5:00 p.m. on Aug 7 (may extend five days if an eligible incumbent does not file). Elections Code §§ 10407, 10225.
More information about key election dates will be posted as it becomes available. Interested in running for office? Visit the City of Millbrae Election FAQ or contact the City Clerk’s Office for assistance.

### Endorse Bob
Add your name to a growing list of neighbors who back responsible, balanced leadership for District 4.
- 02
### Put Up a Yard Sign
Show your support where neighbors will see it — we'll drop off a sign and help you set it up.
- 03
### Talk to Your Neighbors
A conversation with people you already know is the most trusted way to spread the word.
- 04
